newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil recovery seen driven by consumer credit.
newsitem.headline: Brazil recovery seen driven by consumer credit.

text.p: Brazil's economic recovery in the final months of 1996 appears to be driven by consumer credit, but the government sees no need to impose restrictions, a senior Finance Ministry official said Thursday.
Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros, economic policy secretary at the ministry, told reporters that consumer habits appeared to have changed with the slowing of inflation.
He said credit purchases have surged because consumers no longer needed to wait for 13-month salary payments at Christmas to make seasonal purchases.
"Why wait when you can buy now," he said.
Mendonca de Barros said he saw no reason for concern in spite of October's record trade deficit of $1.308 billion,
"I am convinced this will come back to earth without the need for direct government intervention," he said.
The government has been pursuing a gradual process of credit-easing in order to bring down interest rates after tight restrictions were clamped on credit last year to halt a consumer boom.
Recently, authorities have asked supermarket chains to show restraint after some retailers offered buyers three-month credit on predated checks.
Finance Minister Pedro Malan, in an interview on Monday with Reuters, said it seemed inappropriate to offer credit with such a long maturity on perishable products.
"We approached them because we didn't want them to get into trouble and then say the government hadn't warned them," Malan said.
